> [!NOTE] > ## Other AI code review bot(s) detected > > CodeRabbit has detected other AI code review bot(s) in this pull request and will avoid duplicating their findings in the review comments. This may lead to a less comprehensive review. ## Walkthrough Expired S3/TTL entries are now deleted with stricter error handling; expired-entry deletions are deferred until after listing using a non-cancelable context. Proto, client, server, S3 handlers, MQ, and shell callers were updated to propagate optional empty-parent-directory cleanup and stop-path parameters. ## Changes | Cohort / File(s) | Change Summary | |---|---| | **Core Filer Logic**
`weed/filer/filer.go` | FindEntry: surfaced delete errors for expired S3/TTL entries; doListDirectoryEntries: collect expired entries during iteration, perform deletions after iteration with a non-cancelable opCtx, track deletedCount, and conditionally trigger empty-parent cleanup with improved stopAtPath logic. | | **Proto Definitions**
`weed/pb/filer.proto` | Added `bool delete_empty_parent_directories = 10` and `string delete_empty_parent_directories_stop_path = 11` to `DeleteEntryRequest`. | | **gRPC Client Code**
`weed/pb/filer_pb/filer_client.go` | Extended `DoRemove` signature with `deleteEmptyParentDirectories bool` and `stopPath string`; updated internal callers; added `DoDeleteEmptyParentDirectories` helper to recursively remove empty parents with stop-path validation and a checked set. | | **gRPC Server Implementation**
`weed/server/filer_grpc_server.go` | DeleteEntry now returns early on errors; on successful delete optionally calls `DeleteEmptyParentDirectories` using a non-cancelable context and the provided/fallback stop path. | | **S3 API Deletion Handlers**
`weed/s3api/s3api_object_handlers_delete.go` | Single- and multi-object Delete handlers now use `DoRemove` with an op-scoped non-cancelable context, compute `deleteEmptyDirs`, defer and aggregate parent-directory cleanup, and replace prior per-object inline cleanup. | | **Consumer Group Storage**
`weed/mq/offset/consumer_group_storage.go` | `DeleteConsumerGroupOffset` now passes the two new trailing `DoRemove` parameters: `false`, `""`. | | **Shell Commands**
`weed/shell/command_remote_unmount.go` | Updated `DoRemove` invocation to include the two new trailing parameters: `false`, `""`. | ## Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant GRPC as Filer gRPC participant Filer participant Store Client->>GRPC: DeleteEntry(path, delete_empty_parent_directories, stop_path) GRPC->>Filer: DoRemove(parent, name, ..., deleteEmptyParentDirectories, stopPath) Note right of Filer: use opCtx (non-cancelable) for store ops Filer->>Store: attempt delete (doDeleteEntryMetaAndData / DeleteOneEntry) using opCtx alt deletion succeeded Filer-->>GRPC: success alt deleteEmptyParentDirectories == true GRPC->>Filer: DoDeleteEmptyParentDirectories(dirPath, stopAtPath) loop ascend parents Filer->>Store: List(parent, limit=1) to check emptiness alt empty Filer->>Store: DoRemove(parentDir, name="", ...) to delete parent else not empty Filer-->>Filer: stop cleanup end end end else deletion failed Filer-->>GRPC: return error end GRPC-->>Client: DeleteEntryResponse ``` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Lister as doListDirectoryEntries participant Filer participant Store Lister->>Store: iterate entries (stream) loop per entry Store-->>Lister: entry Lister->>Lister: check expiration (S3 TTL or TTL) alt expired Lister->>Lister: collect expiredEntry (defer deletion) else valid Lister-->>Lister: keep entry in results end end Lister->>Filer: batch delete collected expired entries using opCtx (non-cancelable) loop per expiredEntry alt S3 expired Filer->>Store: doDeleteEntryMetaAndData(opCtx) else TTL expired Filer->>Store: DeleteOneEntry(opCtx) end end alt deletedCount>0 and no valid entries and first page Filer->>Filer: DeleteEmptyParentDirectories(opCtx, stopAtPath) end ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~75 minutes - Review focus: - S3 expiry deletion error semantics in `weed/filer/filer.go`. - Non-cancelable context creation/use (opCtx) to ensure cleanup runs correctly. - Boundary checks and validation in `DoDeleteEmptyParentDirectories`. - Propagation of new proto fields and updated `DoRemove` signature across call sites. ## Possibly related PRs - seaweedfs/seaweedfs#7426 — Very close: similar S3 TTL expiry deletion flow, deferred deletions, and empty-parent-directory cleanup changes. - seaweedfs/seaweedfs#7402 — Related: modifies filer deletion flow and may interact with deferred deletion semantics. ## Poem > 🐇 I hopped through entries, nudged the ones grown old, > Collected sleepy bytes and marched them out bold. > I climbed each parent door and swept the rooms so neat, > Tidied paths and stopped where rules and stop-paths meet. > A gentle hop, a tidy trail — the filesystem feels sweet. ## Pre-merge checks and finishing touches

The required threshold is 80.00%. | You can run `@coderabbitai generate docstrings` to improve docstring coverage. |
✅ Passed checks (2 passed) | Check name | Status | Explanation | | :---------------: | :------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Title check | ✅ Passed | The PR title 'S3: Also delete parent directory if empty' clearly and concisely describes the main feature being added: S3-related functionality to delete empty parent directories during object deletion. | | Description check | ✅ Passed | The PR description covers all required template sections: problem statement (data inconsistency from client-side cleanup), solution (server-side filer gRPC service cleanup), and testing approach (integration tests). The description is complete and provides meaningful context. |

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

## Summary of Changes Hello @chrislusf, I'm Gemini Code Assist[^1]! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed! This pull request addresses potential data inconsistencies by centralizing the cleanup of empty parent directories within the filer gRPC service. It also refines S3 object expiration to leverage modification times for lifecycle-managed objects and introduces new gRPC parameters for controlled recursive directory deletion. These changes improve the robustness and accuracy of file and directory management, especially for S3-compatible operations. ### Highlights * **Centralized Empty Directory Cleanup**: The responsibility for cleaning up empty parent directories has been moved from client-side logic to the filer gRPC service. This change aims to prevent data inconsistencies that could arise from client-side cleanup. * **S3 Lifecycle Expiration Improvements**: S3 object expiration logic has been enhanced to correctly use the modification time (Mtime) for objects with S3 expiry enabled, rather than the creation time (Crtime). This ensures more accurate lifecycle management for S3-compatible storage. * **New Filer gRPC Delete Options**: The `DeleteEntryRequest` protobuf message now includes new fields (`delete_empty_parent_directories` and `delete_empty_parent_directories_stop_path`) to control recursive deletion of empty parent directories directly via the filer service. * **Recursive TTL Updates for S3 Lifecycle**: New utility functions have been introduced in the S3 API server to recursively update the Time-To-Live (TTL) and S3 expiry flags for all entries within a directory, supporting S3 bucket lifecycle rules.

Using Gemini Code Assist
The full guide for Gemini Code Assist can be found on our [documentation page](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-github-code), here are some quick tips. Invoking Gemini You can request assistance from Gemini at any point by creating a comment using either `/gemini ` or `@gemini-code-assist `. Below is a summary of the supported commands on the current page. Feature | Command | Description --- | --- | --- Code Review | `/gemini review` | Performs a code review for the current pull request in its current state. Pull Request Summary | `/gemini summary` | Provides a summary of the current pull request in its current state. Comment | @gemini-code-assist | Responds in comments when explicitly tagged, both in pull request comments and review comments. Help | `/gemini help` | Displays a list of available commands. Customization To customize Gemini Code Assist for GitHub experience, repository maintainers can create a configuration file and/or provide a custom code review style guide (such as PEP-8 for Python) by creating and adding files to a `.gemini/` folder in the base of the repository. Detailed instructions can be found [here](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/customize-gemini-behavior-github). Limitations & Feedback Gemini Code Assist may make mistakes. Please leave feedback on any instances where its feedback is incorrect or counter productive. You can react with :thumbsup: and :thumbsdown: on @gemini-code-assist comments. If you're interested in giving your feedback about your experience with Gemini Code Assist for Github and other Google products, sign up [here](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2cyuGuTWsEw84yG). You can also get AI-powered code generation, chat, as well as code reviews directly in the IDE at no cost with the [Gemini Code Assist IDE Extension](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini/code-assist).
